lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Ernesto, it's Luis from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Luis. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walking went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good. Busy, but good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What happened with the walking?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Some days yes, some days no. Maybe 3.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you try the mall?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd do it if the day had a few more hours.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I like what I eat. I'm not going to change at my age.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, being so tired makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Three 10-minute walks count the same as one 30-minute walk.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I don't really see the point.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: When I walk I sleep better, I noticed that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You said the same thing last week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know, I know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know, I know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not sure it's worth it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Three 10-minute walks count the same as one 30-minute walk.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, my granddaughter is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your family is a big part of why.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Next week I want you to walk 20 minutes on 3 days.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 7. Maybe 8.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 7 and not a 4?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll go to the mall instead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Adds conditional meaning not clearly stated by participant
Wants to keep up with grandkids
Repeats info after resistance, no permission
Says he can manage three days
Sets goal for him without collaboration

flags.reason: Directive 'You have to make this a priority' without permission; increases resistance.
Calls out repetition ('You said the same thing last week'), which can feel judgmental and triggers defensiveness.
Health warning pushes change without permission; participant responds with disengaged 'I know, I know'.
Participant's motivation about keeping up with grandkids was not reflected or explored; coach moved on.
Prescribed 20-minute, 3-day goal without asking permission or collaborating on the goal.

score.summary: Coach used several persuasive and directive moves (lines 14, 27, 29, 43) that met resistance, and the participant's change talk about grandchildren and sleep went largely unreflected. The call did reach a concrete, self-chosen plan at the end, with good use of scaling and barrier planning.
strengths: Line 20: complex reflection named the ambivalence between fatigue and wanting to make this work.
Line 37: affirmed the participant's own problem solving ('You figured that out on your own').
Line 24: emphasized autonomy ('It's completely your call'), which helped reduce resistance.
Line 45-49: scaling question followed by 'Why a 7 and not a 4?' drew out his confidence and plan.
coaching_tips: Replace 'You have to make this a priority' (line 14) with a reflection or open question about what priority means to him.
Reflect the change talk in line 21 (grandkids) and line 26 (better sleep) before offering any new idea.
Drop the health warning in line 29 and the 'You said the same thing last week' comment in line 27; use reflections instead.
Ask permission before setting the goal in line 43, e.g., 'Would it help to talk through a walking goal for next week?'
Summarize the conversation before closing, and check his feelings at the start of the call.
